Helping children develop with confidence and joy
Mr Euan Macdonald
Headteacher
Welcome to Northstar Nurture School, a specialist provision supporting children and young people aged 7 to 16 with autism and complex additional needs. We are committed to providing a safe, nurturing and highly structured environment where every pupil is valued, understood and supported to achieve their full potential.
Our personalised curriculum is built around three flexible pathways Discover, Navigate and Journey ensuring that learning is carefully matched to each pupil’s developmental stage, communication needs and emotional readiness. This approach enables pupils to make meaningful progress in engagement, communication, emotional regulation, independence and academic learning.
At Northstar, we place strong emphasis on wellbeing, positive relationships and high-quality teaching. Therapeutic approaches are embedded across the school day, supporting pupils to access learning and develop the skills they need for life beyond the classroom. Progress is measured holistically, recognising growth in confidence, independence, communication and personal development alongside academic achievement.
We work in close partnership with families, professionals and external agencies to ensure a joined-up approach to each child’s Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). Together, we strive to provide consistently high standards of care, education and support, enabling every pupil to thrive.
We are proud of our nurturing ethos, our skilled and dedicated staff team, and our commitment to supporting every child on their unique learning journey.
Why Northstar Nurture School ?
NorthStar Nurture School Curriculum Statement
Guiding Every Learner on Their Unique Educational Journey
At Northstar Nurture School Nurture School, education is not a static process, but a living, evolving journey. We recognise that every child comes to us with their own story, abilities, and aspirations. Our curriculum is carefully crafted to honour this diversity, ensuring each learner is met with curiosity, confidence, and unwavering support. We believe that learning is most meaningful when it moves in rhythm with the unique pace and needs of each child.
Curriculum Philosophy: A Journey Tailored to the Individual
At the heart of Northstar Nurture School’s ethos is the conviction that learning should be a collaborative and transformative adventure. Our curriculum is built to meet each student exactly where they are in their development, and to travel with them as they grow in understanding and capability. Rather than a one-size-fits-all model, we provide three flexible learning pathways Discover, Navigate, and Journey each designed to nurture specific stages of educational and personal growth.
Flexible Learning Pathways
This initial pathway is for children just beginning to engage with learning and the wider world. Here, our focus is on igniting curiosity and building the very foundations of learning.Through sensory experiences, hands-on exploration, and playful interaction, our studentsbegin to:
• Persist in activities, even when they are challenging
• Anticipate outcomes and build a sense of cause and effect
• Gain the confidence to take initiative and experiment
The Discover pathway is about opening the door to wonder helping children feel safe, valued, and ready to take their first steps on the learning journey
As children grow, their capacity for communication, focus, and social interaction strengthens. The Navigate pathway is designed for these learners, emphasising:
• Language development and expressive communication
• Emotional awareness and understanding
• Cooperative play and teamwork
• Self-regulation strategies for managing feelings and behaviour
Learners are gently encouraged to chart their own direction, find their voice, and connect with peers and adults. This stage is about developing the tools to participate, express, andrelate.
In the Journey pathway, children are becoming increasingly independent. They engage in a holistic blend of academic study, therapeutic input, and personal development. The focus here is on:
• Problem-solving and critical thinking
• Social interaction and understanding group dynamics
• Organisational skills and setting personal goals
• Exploration of leisure interests and hobbies
Journey is about stepping confidently into new opportunities, making choices, and building autonomy for life beyond the classroom.
Our curriculum is broad, balanced, and enriched with therapeutic support. We are committed to providing every pupil, regardless of their starting point, with access to the fundamental areas of learning, including:
• Literacy and Numeracy: Essential reading, writing, speaking, and mathematical skills form the core of academic growth.
• Science and Investigation: Children are encouraged to ask questions, experiment, and discover the world through hands-on inquiry.
• PSHE and SMSC: Personal, Social, Health and Economic education, along with Spiritual, Moral, Social, and Cultural development, ensure well-rounded growth.
• Creative Arts: Opportunities for artistic and musical expression help children communicate and connect with their world.
• Communication and Regulation – SCERTS: Developing the ability to communicate needs, desires, and ideas, while learning to manage emotions and behaviour.
• Physical and Sensory OT: Movement, physical health, and sensory experiences are integrated into daily learning, informed by occupational therapy.
• Life Skills and Independence (OT): Practical skills for daily living, personal care, and growing independence are prioritised for every learner.
Therapeutic support is seamlessly woven through all areas, ensuring that progress in one domain supports and enhances development in others.
At NorthStar, we see learning not simply as the acquisition of facts, but as the shaping of minds, hearts, and character. Our teaching approach is deeply personalised:
• We view every child as a unique individual, with their own strengths, interests, and needs.
• Teaching is adaptive and flexible, responding to each child’s pace and style of learning.
• The environment is safe, nurturing, and stimulating, encouraging risk-taking and resilience.
• Our staff are skilled not only in teaching, but in building trusting relationships that underpin all learning.
The SCERTS framework (Social Communication, Emotional Regulation, and Transactional Support) underpins much of our practice, especially in autism-specific classes. This evidencebased approach supports children to develop their communication, emotional regulation, and social understanding, while empowering staff to tailor strategies to individual needs.
We believe education is most effective as a shared journey. Parents, carers, therapists, and teachers are essential partners, collaborating to ensure consistency, coherence, and depth of learning. Regular communication, joint planning, and mutual respect ensure each child is truly known, heard, and supported.
At NorthStar Nurture School, we want every child to flourish not only academically, but as awhole person. Our aspirations are clear:
• Curious: Inspired to ask questions, explore, and seek out new experiences
• Resilient: Equipped to face challenges, adapt, and bounce back from difficulties
• Independent: Confident in making choices, setting goals, and taking ownership of learning
• Connected: Able to build authentic relationships, communicate effectively, and find their voice
Above all, we want pupils to feel valued, empowered, and proud of every achievement— large or small.
Every child’s Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) is the starting point for their personalised learning programme. Targets are carefully crafted around each learner’s developmental readiness, interests, and strengths, ensuring that progress is both meaningful and achievable. While the school community explores shared themes each term to foster unity and belonging, each pupil’s plan defines how they access and engage with these themes.
This approach guarantees learning remains relevant and motivating.
Our teaching and learning are:
• Collaborative: Teachers, therapists, families, and the child work together to shape goals and strategies.
• Flexible: Plans are continually adjusted based on progress, wellbeing, and emerging needs.
• Reflective: Regular observation, discussion, and review ensure learning stays dynamic and responsive.
Beyond the classroom, we enrich education with visits to local places of interest, outdoor adventures, and special immersion days. These experiences extend learning, build life skills, and help children make real-world connections.
The expertise and passion of our staff are the foundation of NorthStar’s success. Our teachers, therapists, and support staff bring deep knowledge in special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), autism, therapy, and emotional wellbeing. Their collective skills create an environment that is not just supportive, but truly inspiring.
• Building strong foundations in reading, writing, speaking, and numeracy
• Developing robust social and emotional skills for life
• Equipping children with transferable life skills for independence and future opportunities
Progress at NorthStar is measured not only by academic milestones, but by each child’s growth in communication, independence, confidence, and most importantly joy in learning. We celebrate every step forward, recognising that for our learners, success is as much about self-belief and wellbeing as it is about knowledge

ABOUT US
At Northstar Nurture School, education is not a static process, but a living, evolving journey. We recognise that every child comes to us with their own story, abilities and aspirations. Our curriculum is carefully crafted to honour this diversity, ensuring each learner is met with curiosity, confidence, and unwavering support. We believe that learning is most meaningful when it moves in rhythm with the unique pace and needs of each child.
Our Aim
At Northstar Nurture School, we aim to:
Develop communication, emotional regulation and social understanding
Build independence, resilience and confidence
Our Curriculum Approach
We believe that our curriculum at Northstar Nurture School:
Celebrates progress and achievement
Meets statutory and legal educational requirements
Our Provision
Northstar Nurture School is a specialist day provision for pupils aged 7 to 16 with autism and complex additional needs whose needs cannot be fully met within mainstream settings. All pupils have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) or are in the process of statutory assessment for an EHCP.
Teaching and learning enable pupils to make sense of the world and to develop the communication, emotional understanding and life skills needed to participate more fully in learning and daily life.
Leadership and Quality of Provision
Northstar Nurture School is led by Mr Euan Macdonald, Proprietor and Headteacher, who brings significant experience in the leadership of specialist provisions. Mr Macdonald is the proprietor of another school that has been judged outstanding by Ofsted, providing strong assurance of high standards, safeguarding and secure leadership.
The leadership team has established clear systems for curriculum delivery, staff training, safeguarding and quality assurance. These systems ensure consistent, responsive practice, with teaching, therapeutic support and pastoral care working together to provide a well-structured learning experience for pupils.
Alongside the Headteacher, the Deputy Headteacher supports the leadership and development of the school. As part of the senior leadership team, Mr Domenico Cusumano has supported the establishment of the school and the implementation of curriculum pathways, therapeutic approaches and operational systems, contributing to a consistent and personalised approach to provision.
The teaching and support team includes staff who have previously worked together within successful specialist and alternative provision settings. This shared experience supports high expectations, effective teamwork and a strong understanding of the needs of pupils with autism and complex additional needs.
The school has been carefully developed to provide a calm, structured and nurturing environment, enabling pupils to feel safe, build confidence and make meaningful progress.
Safeguarding Statement
At Northstar Nurture School, safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children is our highest priority. We are committed to providing a safe, caring and secure environment in which pupils are protected from harm and able to learn and thrive.
Safeguarding is the responsibility of all adults working in or with the school. Robust policies, procedures and training ensure that safeguarding practice is consistent and compliant with statutory guidance and local authority requirements.
Staff are trained to recognise behaviour as a form of communication and to respond appropriately to concerns, particularly in relation to pupils with autism and complex needs.
Designated Safeguarding Leads
The school’s leadership and governance arrangements reflect a clear understanding of safeguarding responsibilities. Ofsted noted that leaders, including the proprietor, have completed appropriate safeguarding and safer recruitment training and have established systems to identify, record and respond to safeguarding concerns.
Northstar Nurture School works in partnership with families, local authorities and external agencies, including social care and health professionals, to safeguard and promote the welfare of pupils through effective information sharing and collaborative working.

ADMISSIONS
Northstar Nurture School - pupil consultation
Upon receiving the consultation paperwork, leaders at Northstar Nurture review all the submitted paperwork to evaluate whether the school is likely to be able meet the student’s needs.
List of paperwork requested by the school:
Referral Documentation from Local Authority
☐ Completed referral form (from LA)
☐ Recent annual review reports
School’s Internal Assessment & Response
☐ Safeguarding information checklist
☐ Record of contact with current/previous school
Supporting Documents
☐ Attendance record from current/previous school
☐ Behaviour logs/reports
☐ Attainment data/progress reports
☐ Individual Health Care Plans (if applicable)
☐ Parental/carer consent forms
Communication & Meeting Records
Transition Preparation (where proceeding)
☐ Transition plan template
☐ Pupil induction checklist
☐ Welcome pack for parents/carers
Referral Journey
If school leaders feel that needs may be met, an initial offer to assess the student is made to the referring local authority. Assessment can take place at the student’s current school or home. Following this, a visit to the school for half a day is offered where the school feels able to meet needs. There may be another visit to the school where more information is required ahead of making a decision.
Where all parties agree placement, an offer of placement is sent to the local authority. Within the first term at Northstar Nurture, we arrange for a review to be held with all stakeholders. Within this meeting, the student’s settling and/or progress is discussed and any necessary amendments or changes to the placement are agreed with the local authority.
